title: In Hebrews 7 In What Ways Does The Eternal Nature Of Christs Priesthood Provide Comfort And Assurance To Believers
paragraphs: The Eternal Priesthood of Christ: Comfort and Assurance for Believers (Hebrews 7)

The book of Hebrews presents a profound portrait of Jesus Christ as our eternal High Priest, surpassing the Old Testament priesthood of Aaron. Nowhere is this more clearly articulated than in Hebrews 7, where the writer emphasizes the unending, unchangeable nature of Christ’s priesthood after the order of Melchizedek. This truth provides deep comfort and unwavering assurance to all who trust in Him. Let’s explore how.
1. Christ’s Priesthood Is Unchanging and Permanent
Unlike the Levitical priests, who were subject to death and had to be replaced, Jesus’ priesthood is eternal and untransferable. The author of Hebrews writes:

And they indeed have been made priests many in number, because that by death they are hindered from continuing: but he, because he abideth for ever, hath his priesthood unchangeable. - Hebrews 7:23-24 ASV

This means that Jesus will never be replaced. He is always able to represent us before God. The permanence of His priesthood assures us that our relationship with God is secure—not dependent on human frailty but on Christ’s eternal life.
2. He Lives to Intercede for Us
One of the most comforting truths in Hebrews 7 is that Jesus continually intercedes for believers:
Wherefore also he is able to save to the uttermost them that draw near unto God through him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them. - Hebrews 7:25 ASV

Unlike earthly priests who eventually die and can no longer fulfill their duties, Jesus’ intercession is eternal. He is always present before the Father, advocating on our behalf. This ongoing intercession gives believers confidence that our salvation is complete and secure, not just at the moment of conversion but forever.
3. A Perfect and Sinless High Priest
Hebrews further highlights the perfection of Jesus’ priesthood:

For such a high priest became us, holy, guileless, undefiled, separated from sinners, and made higher than the heavens; who needeth not daily, like those high priests, to offer up sacrifices, first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people: for this he did once for all, when he offered up himself. - Hebrews 7:26-27 ASV

Jesus never needs to atone for His own sins—He is sinless and completely holy. His sacrifice is entirely sufficient for all who believe. This assures us that our forgiveness is not partial or temporary, but complete and everlasting.
4. Assurance Grounded in God’s Oath and Promise
The writer emphasizes that Christ’s priesthood was established with an oath from God Himself:
(for they indeed have been made priests without an oath; but he with an oath by him that saith of him, The Lord sware and will not repent himself, Thou art a priest for ever)... - Hebrews 7:21 ASV
God’s unchanging promise undergirds Christ’s eternal priesthood. Our assurance rests not on our feelings or performance, but on God’s unbreakable word and faithfulness.
5. Salvation to the Uttermost

Because Christ’s priesthood is eternal, He is able to save completely—“to the uttermost”—everyone who comes to God through Him (Hebrews 7:25 ASV). There is no limit to His saving power, no expiration on His ministry, and no circumstance too great for His intercession.
Practical Implications for Believers
Security: Our salvation and standing before God are secure, anchored in Christ’s eternal ministry.
Confidence in Prayer: We can boldly approach God, knowing Jesus continually intercedes for us (Hebrews 4:16 ASV).
Freedom from Fear: No sin, failure, or weakness can undo the work of our eternal High Priest (Romans 8:34 ASV).
Conclusion

The eternal nature of Christ’s priesthood is not just a theological concept—it is the foundation of our comfort and assurance. Jesus, our unchanging and perfect High Priest, forever intercedes for us, guaranteeing our salvation and drawing us near to God with confidence.
